project.name: Kujo
project.tagline: Real examples. Recorded execution. Clear limits.

cards.title: Bounded work
cards.tagline: Limit concurrent batch work to two jobs.
cards.label: Built with Kujo
cards.alt: Built with Kujo: Bounded work. Limit concurrent batch work to two jobs.
cards.caption:
I like being able to put a limit right next to the work. In Kujo, parallel_map takes the inputs, a function, and a concurrency limit. Here it doubles four values with at most two jobs at a time. Await it and get the results back in order.

https://github.com/kujolang/kujo/blob/2cfaf185ad03059c89ef4f72fb061074255d00fc/examples/test_parallel_simple.kujo
cards.notes: A batch of jobs should not turn into an unbounded pile of work. Reduced the canonical parallel_map example to four inputs and a limit of two. This verifies results and ordering, not a speedup. Output shown here, when present, was observed in evidence/verified/bounded-map/stdout.txt. Full commands and artifacts are in the verification report.

cards.title: Read it twice
cards.tagline: Await the same task result more than once.
cards.label: Built with Kujo
cards.alt: Built with Kujo: Read it twice. Await the same task result more than once.
cards.caption:
Run the task once. Read the result wherever you need it. Kujo lets you await the same task handle more than once, so a second reader gets the completed result too. Six lines that make task coordination a little less annoying.

https://github.com/kujolang/kujo/blob/2cfaf185ad03059c89ef4f72fb061074255d00fc/tests/language_task_contracts.rs
cards.notes: Reading a completed task once should not consume its result. Extracted the reusable-completion contract into a standalone example. Both waits return 21; cancelling the completed task returns false. Output shown here, when present, was observed in evidence/verified/reusable-task/stdout.txt. Full commands and artifacts are in the verification report.

cards.title: Stop a task
cards.label: Built with Kujo
cards.alt: Built with Kujo: Stop a task. Stop cooperative work; handle rejection.
cards.caption:
Start a task, wait until it is running, cancel it, handle the result. This is what cooperative task cancellation looks like in Kujo. The stop path lives right alongside the work, where the next developer can actually find it.

https://github.com/kujolang/kujo/blob/2cfaf185ad03059c89ef4f72fb061074255d00fc/tests/concurrency_lifecycle_contracts.rs
cards.notes: A background task needs a deliberate stop path. Reduced the lifecycle cancellation contract. The shared started flag prevents a start/cancel race. Cancellation is cooperative; this does not promise interruption of arbitrary blocking native calls. Output shown here, when present, was observed in evidence/verified/cancel-task/stdout.txt. Full commands and artifacts are in the verification report.

cards.title: Stable JSON
cards.tagline: Stable JSON, even when key order changes.
cards.label: Built with Kujo
cards.alt: Built with Kujo: Stable JSON. Stable JSON, even when key order changes.
cards.caption:
Same data, different key order, identical JSON. Kujo sorts dictionary keys when it serializes them, including nested dictionaries. Handy when you want generated files to produce useful diffs instead of rearranging themselves every run.

https://github.com/kujolang/kujo/blob/2cfaf185ad03059c89ef4f72fb061074255d00fc/examples/helper_hlp_015_canonical_json.kujo
cards.notes: Dictionary insertion order creates noisy diffs and unstable machine output. Reduced the canonical HLP-015 example to nested key ordering and equality. Output shown here, when present, was observed in evidence/verified/canonical-json/stdout.txt. Full commands and artifacts are in the verification report.

cards.title: Read the exit
cards.tagline: Read exit status without parsing text.
cards.label: Built with Kujo
cards.alt: Built with Kujo: Read the exit. Read exit status without parsing text.
cards.caption:
Running commands from code gets easier when the result has fields. Kujo gives you stdout, exit status, timeout, and truncation flags. Here I run a command and check the result directly. Small thing, but useful in an agent tool loop.

https://github.com/kujolang/kujo/blob/2cfaf185ad03059c89ef4f72fb061074255d00fc/examples/helper_hlp_013_process_result.kujo
cards.notes: Shell text alone does not tell an agent whether a process timed out or failed. Adapted HLP-013 from rustc --version to a portable printf command. Checks success and exitcode, then prints structured output, timeout and truncation flags. Output shown here, when present, was observed in evidence/verified/process-result/stdout.txt. Full commands and artifacts are in the verification report.

cards.title: Safer output
cards.tagline: Redact secrets in print and JSON output.
cards.label: Built with Kujo
cards.alt: Built with Kujo: Safer output. Redact secrets in print and JSON output.
cards.caption:
I still use print to debug things. Kujo lets me wrap a value with secret() so it shows up as *** in terminal output and JSON. Here is the whole example. A useful default for values you do not want wandering into logs.

https://github.com/kujolang/kujo/blob/2cfaf185ad03059c89ef4f72fb061074255d00fc/examples/secrets_redaction.kujo
cards.notes: A debug print can accidentally disclose a credential. Reduced the canonical secret example; the dummy value is not a credential. Redaction is not encryption and explicit reveal remains possible. Output shown here, when present, was observed in evidence/verified/secret-output/stdout.txt. Full commands and artifacts are in the verification report.

cards.title: Eval
cards.label: Verified with Kujo
cards.alt: Verified with Kujo: Eval. Turn workflow expectations into checks.
cards.caption:
Here is a small Eval suite you can actually run: check that a command succeeds, that a manifest exists, and that the file clears a size check. Three explicit checks, with JSON results ready for the next step in your workflow.

https://github.com/kujolang/eval/blob/71e66dff780d6930bcbe093c046bf31aa26411df/examples/release_gate_suite.json
cards.notes: A successful command alone is not a complete release smoke check. Executed the unchanged canonical three-check release suite against its copied kennel.toml fixture. This checks a command, file existence, and file size; it does not evaluate model quality. Output shown here, when present, was observed in evidence/verified/eval/stdout.txt. Full commands and artifacts are in the verification report.

cards.title: Workcell
cards.tagline: Review execution policy before work starts.
cards.label: Verified with Kujo
cards.alt: Verified with Kujo: Workcell. Review execution policy before work starts.
cards.caption:
I want to review the settings before agent work starts. Workcell can show the resolved network policy, filesystem settings, and resource limits from one definition. This example uses inspect to make that preflight easy to read.

https://github.com/kujolang/workcell/blob/189d7ab6e975301a0e5100b65e8ad3fe4a584573/examples/hello/workcell.json
cards.notes: Execution settings are hard to review when they are buried in launch commands. Executed validate and inspect --summary on the unchanged hello definition. No container was launched; Docker was unavailable. Network none and resource limits are resolved policy, not observed enforcement. Output shown here, when present, was observed in evidence/verified/workcell/stdout.txt. Full commands and artifacts are in the verification report.

cards.title: PackWrite
cards.tagline: Check the handoff before the next agent.
cards.label: Verified with Kujo
cards.alt: Verified with Kujo: PackWrite. Check the handoff before the next agent.
cards.caption:
Before handing a pack to the next agent, check that it is complete. PackWrite validates the files and reports the phase count and anything missing. This six-phase sample is a quick way to try the workflow locally.

https://github.com/kujolang/packwrite/blob/721dcc0ad41eaedc159d84f34a06396f92ede79f/README.md#commands
cards.notes: An incomplete agent pack can send the next session into guesswork. Executed validate and summary on the released golden-agent fixture with six phases. The fixture is a test input, not newly generated model output. No provider was called. Output shown here, when present, was observed in evidence/verified/packwrite/stdout.txt. Full commands and artifacts are in the verification report.

cards.caption:
Agent work should leave something useful after the chat closes. With RunLedger I can start a run, record how it finished, and write a report. The receipt stays in the repo workflow, ready for the next person picking up the work.

https://github.com/kujolang/runledger/blob/ab0ec5d2edb7ffd913f48d092aa6fc17cab58d13/README.md#quick-start
cards.notes: An agent session ends, and its run context disappears into chat history. Executed a scripted receipt lifecycle using provider local and model scripted-example. Pass is a supplied demonstration verdict. No token usage, costs, model invocation, or automated quality judgment is claimed. Output shown here, when present, was observed in evidence/verified/runledger/stdout.txt. Full commands and artifacts are in the verification report.

cards.title: Lens
cards.tagline: Check desktop and mobile; keep evidence.
cards.label: Verified with Kujo
cards.alt: Verified with Kujo: Lens. Check desktop and mobile; keep evidence.
cards.caption:
Built a page? Give the next developer more than a screenshot from your laptop. This Lens example checks a local dashboard at desktop and mobile sizes and saves screenshots, browser findings, and a report they can inspect.

https://github.com/kujolang/lens/blob/85778065ca329c93293b387a0e7011437b6d0c60/examples/specs/dashboard.json
cards.notes: A page can look fine at one size and still have console or layout problems. Executed a local dashboard fixture with desktop/mobile screenshots, accessibility and link checks. Adapted the canonical spec by removing unsupported not_exists. No accessibility certification or production-site coverage is claimed. Output shown here, when present, was observed in evidence/verified/lens/stdout.txt. Full commands and artifacts are in the verification report.

cards.title: ShipCheck
cards.label: Verified with Kujo
cards.alt: Verified with Kujo: ShipCheck. Gate on explicit release-readiness checks.
cards.caption:
I would rather put the release checklist in a command than keep it in my head. ShipCheck looks for the repo signals I need before shipping and gives me JSON plus a gate exit code. Here is the small example to try in a local checkout.

https://github.com/kujolang/shipcheck/blob/7eedd9e02d8730d65e06e16f4984d909d23539bc/README.md#gate-semantics
cards.notes: A release checklist is easy to forget when shipping gets busy. Executed gate --format json against the pinned ShipCheck release checkout. This checks repository readiness signals, not test execution, artifact integrity, or release certification. Output shown here, when present, was observed in evidence/verified/shipcheck/stdout.txt. Full commands and artifacts are in the verification report.
